title: Beyond Traditional Use: Mechanistic Insights into the Medicinal Potential of Thymus tiflisiensis and Modulatory Enhancement Effects of Gallic Acid.
authors: Mittova, Valentina; Botchkova, Ekaterina; Tsetskhladze, Zurab R; Eradze, Nino; Motsonelidze, Catherine; Pirtskhalava, Marina; Roviello, Giovanni N
one_liner_zh: 该文研究百里香提取物及没食子酸的抗氧化、抗炎和抗菌活性，仅用分子对接预测与细菌酶的结合，核心是植物药理学而非蛋白质结构计算建模，与本课题关系微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thymus tiflisiensis is used in Georgian traditional medicine, but its pharmacological properties remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the antioxidant, protein denaturation inhibitory, and antibacterial activities of leaf and root extracts and examined the modulatory effects of gallic acid (GA) on these activities. METHODS: Methanolic extracts of leaves and roots were analyzed for total phenolic and flavonoid contents, rosmarinic acid (RA), ascorbic acid, and glutathione. Antioxidant activity was evaluated using the DPPH assay, protein denaturation inhibitory activity using a bovine serum albumin denaturation assay, and antibacterial activity against Streptococcus agalactiae and Escherichia coli using broth microdilution. The combined effects of the plant extracts and GA were evaluated across multiple concentration matrices. Molecular docking was used to predict the interactions of RA and GA with the bacterial enzymes MurF and LpxC. RESULTS: The methanolic leaf extract exhibited greater antioxidant activity (IC(50) = 34.8 microg/mL) than the root extract (IC(50) = 81.9 microg/mL), accompanied by higher total phenolic (113.6 vs. 56.9 mg GAE/g DW) and flavonoid (63.8 vs. 19.0 mg RE/g DW) contents and higher ASC/DHA and GSH/GSSG ratios. Conversely, the root extract exhibited greater protein denaturation inhibitory activity (IC(50) = 51.3 vs. 159.7 microg/mL for the leaf extract) and moderate antibacterial activity against S. agalactiae (MIC = 6.0 mg/mL) and contained higher levels of RA. The addition of 5 microM GA enhanced the antioxidant activity of both leaf and root extracts. In protein denaturation assays, 10 microM GA produced a minor enhancement at low extract concentrations, whereas 100 microM GA reduced the inhibitory effects. At 1 mM, GA enhanced the antibacterial activity of both extracts against S. agalactiae and that of the root extract against E. coli. Molecular docking predicted more favorable interactions of RA with MurF and LpxC than those of GA. CONCLUSIONS: T. tiflisiensis root extracts exhibited greater protein denaturation inhibitory and antibacterial activities, whereas leaf extracts showed greater antioxidant activity. GA modulated these activities in a concentration- and tissue-dependent manner, with enhancement observed at specific concentrations and attenuation at higher concentrations in the protein denaturation assay. Exploratory molecular docking predicted favorable interactions of RA with the bacterial enzymes MurF and LpxC. These findings support further investigation of the bioactive properties of T. tiflisiensis and the mechanisms underlying their modulation by GA.
abstract_zh: 背景：Thymus tiflisiensis 用于格鲁吉亚传统医学，但其药理特性仍缺乏充分表征。本研究评估了叶和根提取物的抗氧化、蛋白质变性抑制及抗菌活性，并考察了没食子酸（GA）对这些活性的调节作用。方法：对叶和根的甲醇提取物进行了总酚和总黄酮含量、迷迭香酸（RA）、抗坏血酸和谷胱甘肽的分析。使用DPPH法评估抗氧化活性，使用牛血清白蛋白变性法评估蛋白质变性抑制活性，并使用肉汤微量稀释法评估对无乳链球菌（Streptococcus agalactiae）和大肠杆菌（Escherichia coli）的抗菌活性。植物提取物与GA的联合效应在多个浓度矩阵中进行了评估。分子对接用于预测RA和GA与细菌酶MurF和LpxC的相互作用。结果：叶的甲醇提取物表现出比根提取物更高的抗氧化活性（IC(50) = 34.8微克/毫升 vs. 81.9微克/毫升），伴随更高的总酚（113.6 vs. 56.9 mg GAE/g DW）和总黄酮（63.8 vs. 19.0 mg RE/g DW）含量，以及更高的ASC/DHA和GSH/GSSG比值。相反，根提取物表现出更高的蛋白质变性抑制活性（IC(50) = 51.3 vs. 叶提取物的159.7微克/毫升）和对无乳链球菌的中等抗菌活性（MIC = 6.0 mg/mL），并含有更高水平的RA。添加5微摩尔GA增强了叶和根提取物的抗氧化活性。在蛋白质变性试验中，10微摩尔GA在低提取物浓度下产生轻微增强，而100微摩尔GA降低了抑制效果。在1毫摩尔浓度下，GA增强了两提取物对无乳链球菌的抗菌活性，以及根提取物对大肠杆菌的抗菌活性。分子对接预测RA与MurF和LpxC的相互作用比GA更有利。结论：T. tiflisiensis 根提取物表现出更高的蛋白质变性抑制和抗菌活性，而叶提取物表现出更高的抗氧化活性。GA以浓度和组织依赖性方式调节这些活性，在蛋白质变性试验中，特定浓度下观察到增强，而较高浓度下则减弱。探索性分子对接预测RA与细菌酶MurF和LpxC存在有利相互作用。这些发现支持对T. tiflisiensis的生物活性特性及其受GA调节的机制进行进一步研究。
